guidance: Feature ONE specific free tool actually published at blackarrow.ltd/tools (a calculator, an audit, an AI builder, or Black Arrow OS — the free pocket CRM). Everything on that page is free value used as a lead magnet. Lead with what the tool tells or gives the owner, cite its stated value where the site shows one, and end with the TOOLS keyword CTA. Rotate through the tools; never feature the same one twice in a row.
evidence_note: Only describe tools/offers actually published on the Black Arrow site.
reason: Exploration (8% budget): sampling 'Offers / Lead Magnets' to keep learning what performs, not just exploiting the current leader.
post_rationale: Single-offer promo cards are the format the brief prefers for one clear ask, and the Revenue Calculator is the least-featured free tool in this cycle's rotation.

guidance: Use a credible external study to explain why a capability matters. Qualified language: 'Research suggests...', 'The study found...'.
evidence_note: Attribute the source. NEVER imply Black Arrow produced the result or achieves the same without evidence.
reason: Balancing the mix: 'Third-Party Research / Market Evidence' was the most under-served eligible category (target 7%, recent 3%).
post_rationale: Carousels lead saves/depth for B2B research content. The speed-to-lead angle is reframed as an honest general pattern from published lead-response research rather than an unverifiable named study, mapped straight to the free Lead Response Audit.

guidance: Honestly handle a common objection or hesitation an owner has about automation/marketing (cost, complexity, 'it feels impersonal'). Build trust. For done-for-you cost objections: never give numbers; the honest answer is that pricing follows a diagnosis meeting.
evidence_note: Transparent and honest; no unsupported guarantees, no done-for-you pricing.
reason: Balancing the mix: 'Objection Handling / Audience Nurture' was the most under-served eligible category (target 6%, recent 3%).
post_rationale: Carousels lead 2026 saves/depth for B2B authority content, and this resolves an unclaimed objection (fear of losing brand voice/control to automation) distinct from the impersonal, cost, timing, complexity, staff-redundancy, tried-and-failed, and data-lock-in objections already shipped.
